sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: JVM internals interview questions show up in every senior Java backend interview — class loading, the runtime memory areas (heap, stack, metaspace), garbage collection (G1, ZGC, Shenandoah, when to pick which), JIT compilation, escape analysis, and the diagnostic tools you reach for in a production incident (jstack, jmap, async-profiler, JFR). This page covers the questions that test depth: "walk me through what happens between System.out.println and the bytes hitting the kernel", "why is this app's tail latency so bad", "how would you tune the GC for a high-throughput service". Each answer is structured for an interview, not a textbook — concept first, then the trade-offs.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
Five mental zones to draw on a whiteboard:

- **Class loader chain** — bootstrap → platform → app → custom.
- **Heap** — young (Eden + survivors) / old; humongous in G1.
- **Metaspace** — class metadata (replaced PermGen in 8).
- **Stacks** — per-thread, frame-per-call.
- **JIT** — C1 (fast compile) + C2 (aggressive optimiser); tiered compilation balances them.

Pick the GC by **goal**: **G1** balanced default, **ZGC / Shenandoah** for sub-ms pauses, **Parallel** for batch.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
The interview surface for this module breaks into these focus areas:

- **Comparisons** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Garbage collection** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Jvm architecture** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Jvm tuning** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Memory analysis** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Profiling and debugging** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Scenario-based** — applied questions tying multiple topics together. Drill these *last*, after the fundamentals are sharp.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **Stop-the-world** is the language; minor pauses on young GC, major on full GC.
- **Escape analysis** can stack-allocate small objects — don't mistake this for guaranteed.
- **OOM is a label, not a cause** — heap, metaspace, native, direct byte buffers each fail differently.
- **JFR / async-profiler** — name the modern tools; `jstack` / `jmap` are your fallback.
- **GC tuning** is mostly **right-sizing the heap** plus picking a collector — most apps need neither.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"The symptom is <pause / OOM / high CPU>. I'd grab a <heap dump | thread dump | flight recording>, look at <retained-size | blocked threads | GC log pauses>, and the suspect is most likely <leak / unbounded cache / wrong GC>. Fix is <code change | -Xmx | switch to G1/ZGC>."*
